'''Paul Couderc''' (15 July 1899 – 5 February 1981) was a French academic who held [[mathematics]] [[professorship]]s at lycées in [[Chartres]] (1926–1929) and [[Paris]] (1930–1944).<ref>{{cite book | chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/referenceworkentry/10.1007/978-0-387-30400-7_308 | doi=10.1007/978-0-387-30400-7_308 | chapter=Couderc, Paul | title=The Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers | year=2007 | last1=Marché | first1=Jordan D. | page=258 | isbn=978-0-387-31022-0 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://scienceworld.wolfram.com/biography/Couderc.html | title=Couderc, Paul (1899-1981) -- from Eric Weisstein's World of Scientific Biography }}</ref>

==Biography==
Couderc completed his education at lycées in [[Nevers]] and [[Dijon]], followed by a [[doctorate]] in mathematical sciences from the [[École normale supérieure|École Normale Supérieure]] in Paris.<ref name="auto">{{cite book | chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/referenceworkentry/10.1007/978-1-4419-9917-7_308 | doi=10.1007/978-1-4419-9917-7_308 | chapter=Couderc, Paul | title=Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers | year=2014 | last1=Marché | first1=Jordan D. | pages=471–472 | isbn=978-1-4419-9916-0 }}</ref> In 1926, he married Blanch Jurus.<ref name="auto"/>

Throughout his career, Couderc authored approximately fifteen works in the field of [[astronomy]].<ref name="auto"/> He provided an interpretation for the phenomena of light echoes around Nova Persei (1901), specifically their perceived superluminal expansion.<ref name="auto"/> This geometrical explanation later found application in the study of [[supernovae]], [[quasar]]s, and [[Gamma-ray burst|γ-ray burst]]s.<ref name="auto"/>

==Awards and recognition==
* [[Kalinga Prize|Kalinga Prize for the Popularization of Science]] (1966)<ref>{{cite book | url=https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb118978620 | title=Couderc }}</ref>
